svg.title: DIA-406 · Tasting From Your Own Pot
svg.desc: Five grids of one hundred squares, each filled to a comprehension quiz score. Two large grids show the randomized trial: engineers who worked without AI scored 67 percent, and engineers who worked with AI scored 50 percent, filled in rust. Three smaller grids sort the AI users by habit: those who generated code and then made themselves understand it scored 86 percent, those who handed the whole job over scored 39 percent, and those who had the AI debug for them scored 24 percent. The habit groups were observed, not assigned, with two to four engineers each.
svg.text: SAME MENU, DIFFERENT KITCHEN · SECTION 6 · THE COOK TASTES FROM HIS OWN POT
THE TRIAL: GROUPS ASSIGNED BY CHANCE
THE AI USERS, SORTED BY HABIT
Observed, not assigned. Two to four engineers
in each group: a pattern, not proof.
Each grid is a comprehension quiz: one hundred points, filled to the score.
The widest gap between the two trial groups was on debugging. Speed did not differ significantly.
52 mostly junior engineers. The two large grids are a randomized trial run by researchers at Anthropic, an AI vendor.
DIA-406 · With AI, engineers scored 50% on comprehension against 67% without. By habit the score ran from 24 to 86.
